spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Passing to sufficiently large height removes the finite correction terms, exposing a clean constant determined by the geometry of the degree-46 polynomial and Richert's B. directed.source_grounded_mathematics: As T0 grows, Y1(t) and Y(t) vanish. The source uses zero-density theorems to assert that most rectangles 3/4≤Re(s)≤1, T0−1≤Im(s)≤T0 are zero-free for sufficiently large T0. Formula (7.2), evaluated with the degree-46 polynomial data, gives a coefficient exceeding (48.1588)^−1 and hence the asymptotic zero-free constant 48.1588.
directed.conceptual_reading: The asymptotic limit separates durable polynomial geometry from secondary finite-height errors. Sparse bad starting rectangles suffice because the contradiction needs a suitable empty seed, not uniform verification of every rectangle.
